recommendation: Keep the audit as-is. Any future desire to make versioned-update assert stricter server enforcement would require a new work-group decision because it would go beyond this clarification.
issue_request: FHIR-34193 was a Published/Persuasive R5 technical correction asking to replace ambiguous versioned-update wording that said the Version ID must be correct for server updates with wording that says servers support version-aware updates and clients specify If-Match for updates.
initial_application: Commit c783e76c54e9e52068af62d0cf99e5c122763459 applied the issue by changing source/http.html and source/capabilitystatement/codesystem-versioning-policy.xml to the requested wording. The current source still contains those changes, and the versioning-policy ValueSet composes the corrected CodeSystem.
additional_context: The linked Zulip discussion confirms that If-Match support should qualify as versioned-update without requiring the server to check client-supplied Resource.meta.versionId. Historical FHIR-11259 introduced the three versioning support levels and older explanatory wording that FHIR-34193 later clarified. Jira and Confluence searches found no later FHIR-core applied or published reversal.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit on the combined branch because no source edit is needed: the active HTTP page and the authoritative terminology source already match the issue request.

related_jiras.note: Introduced the three versioning support levels and the older versioned-update wording that FHIR-34193 later clarified.
